summary: Dog Mountain tower in Stillwater State Forest: 1925 steel tower, 1935 pole tower per firelookout.com; destroyed 1961 or burned early 1960s; sources disagree.

facts.design: Windowed wood-frame cab on a four-legged pole frame (1959 survey); 1925 newspaper items describe a 35-foot steel tower
facts.status_note: Destroyed by fire. Firelookout.com says 1961; a 1967 survey note says it burned about three years earlier.

events.note: Tower in use during the 1924 fire season, per a January 1925 newspaper item. No construction year given in the sources.
Firelookout.com lists a 20-foot pole L-4 tower in 1935. Sources do not say whether it replaced the 1925 steel tower.
Destroyed per firelookout.com. A 1967 survey note says the tower burned about three years earlier.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com dates a 20-foot pole tower to 1935. The 1925 newspaper items describe a 35-foot steel tower already in use in 1924. The story reports both and does not say they are the same structure.
Firelookout.com says destroyed in 1961. The 1967 survey note says it burned about three years earlier. The story reports the disagreement and does not choose a year.
The facts use the 1959 survey's 45-foot overall height (13.7 m) for the cab on pole framework. The 1925 steel tower is described as 35 feet, and the 1935 pole tower as 20 feet.

sources.title: History of the Stillwater State Forest

notes_for_editor: Height 13.7 m in the brief matches the 1959 survey's 45 ft overall for the cab on pole framework; it does not match the 1925 steel tower (35 ft) or the 1935 pole tower (20 ft). Destruction year unresolved: firelookout.com says 1961; the 1967 survey note says about three years before 1967. Cusick gives no date for the tower or for the worker's lookout job. No access or current-site source. Brief had no agency; Montana DNRC added from firelookout.com.
